tier_reason: The repo publishes the harness behind the cuDNN comparison: hopper/benchmark_attn.py (public since tag v2.6.3, 2024-07-25, two weeks after arXiv v1) times FlashAttention-2, Triton, cuDNN (cudnn-frontend pygraph SDPA, fwd and bwd) and FA3 and prints TFLOPS. hopper/setup.py publishes the nvcc flags, and the paper names the toolchain (CUDA 12.3, cuDNN 9.1.1.17, CUTLASS 3.5) and the GPU (H100 80GB SXM5 at a fixed 1830 MHz), so code, compiler, flags and GPU are all public.

corrections.caveats: Retier B to A rests on the repo and the setup stated in the paper. The paper PDF itself could not be reopened in this session (arxiv.org, proceedings.neurips.cc and tridao.me are blocked by the egress proxy); the toolchain versions come from the paper text as quoted by the orchestrator, and the cuDNN 9.1.1.17 appendix line was confirmed only through search snippets. arXiv v2 listed CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.0.0 and CUTLASS 3.3. By search snippets, the NeurIPS/final version's headline numbers are BF16 up to 840 TFLOPs/s (85% utilization) and FP8 1.3 PFLOPs/s, while v1/v2 gave 740 TFLOPs/s (75%) and about 1.2 PFLOPs/s. The public harness's default configuration differs from the paper's (batch_size fixed at 2, seqlen 1k-32k, hidden 2048; the paper sets batch so total tokens = 16k with seqlen 512-16k), so the figures can only be reproduced after editing the script. No tag marks the exact commit used for the paper figures. The FP8 cuDNN harness (hopper/benchmark_flash_attention_fp8.py) is in HEAD but not at v2.6.3. HEAD's hopper/setup.py now downloads nvcc 12.6.85 plus ptxas 12.8.93 and uses different flags, so current builds do not match the paper's toolchain.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Paper: nvcc from CUDA 12.3, CUTLASS 3.5, cuDNN 9.1.1.17, H100 80GB SXM5 at 1830 MHz. hopper/setup.py at tag v2.6.3 (2024-07-25), nvcc: -O3 -std=c++17 -U__CUDA_NO_HALF_OPERATORS__ -U__CUDA_NO_HALF_CONVERSIONS__ -U__CUDA_NO_BFLOAT16_OPERATORS__ -U__CUDA_NO_BFLOAT16_CONVERSIONS__ -U__CUDA_NO_BFLOAT162_OPERATORS__ -U__CUDA_NO_BFLOAT162_CONVERSIONS__ --expt-relaxed-constexpr --expt-extended-lambda --use_fast_math --ptxas-options=--verbose,--register-usage-level=10,--warn-on-local-memory-usage -lineinfo -DCUTLASS_DEBUG_TRACE_LEVEL=0 -DNDEBUG -DQBLKSIZE=128 -DKBLKSIZE=128 -DCTA256 -DDQINRMEM -DEXECMODE=0 -gencode arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a --threads 4; host C++: -O3 -std=c++17.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed venue confirmed: Marot, Pellerin, Remacle, 'One machine, one minute, three billion tetrahedra', International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering 117(9):967-990, 2019, DOI 10.1002/nme.5987. Gmsh's contrib/hxt/README.md and doc/texinfo/gmsh.texi both cite it, and a web search returns the Wiley Online Library listing. The authors are first-party, but the measurement is peer-reviewed, so B stands; there is no public comparison harness or stated compiler and flags, so it is not A.

corrections.caveats: Venue confirmed as Int J Numer Methods Eng 117(9):967-990 (2019), DOI 10.1002/nme.5987 (peer-reviewed; the authors are the Gmsh/HXT developers). The paper states no compiler or flags. contrib/hxt/README.md recommends building with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release and -march=native (C and CXX flags) and says `Delaunay_CLI -sv2 -G10000000` gives logs very similar to Table 2 of the paper, but that reproduces only the HXT side. The CGAL/TetGen/Geogram comparison harness is not in the repo, and those README flags are recommendations, not the stated paper build.
